_description: Real literature-search counts behind eMethods S9 / the 'Evidence before this study' statement (Task 3, reviewer #3). Replaces the [n - to confirm] placeholders. No number in this file is invented or estimated: every non-null count was obtained by actually running the exact search string named in eMethods S9 against the live database API/interface on run_date, or is a documented, reproducible researcher judgment applied to the real retrieved record lists (marked as such). Numbers that could not be obtained honestly are null with a reason.
run_date_note: The search string specifies 'database inception to July 19, 2026' as the search window. This file was actually executed on 2026-08-03 (run_date), 15 days after that cutoff, because record-level logging was not captured at the time of the original search (see eMethods S9). Every query below applies an explicit upper date bound of 2026-07-19 so the returned counts reflect the stated search window and are not inflated by records published between 2026-07-19 and the run date.

pubmed.query: ("large language model*"[tiab] OR "large language models"[tiab] OR LLM[tiab] OR LLMs[tiab] OR GPT*[tiab] OR "generative pretrained transformer*"[tiab] OR "foundation model*"[tiab]) AND ("brain-computer interface*"[tiab] OR "brain computer interface*"[tiab] OR BCI[tiab] OR BCIs[tiab] OR "P300 speller*"[tiab] OR "P300-based speller*"[tiab] OR "augmentative and alternative communication"[tiab] OR AAC[tiab])
pubmed.access_method: NCBI E-utilities esearch (https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esearch.fcgi), db=pubmed, datetype=pdat, mindate=1900/01/01, maxdate=2026/07/19. Exact string above passed verbatim (URL-encoded) as the term parameter.
pubmed.provenance: Live query executed 2026-08-03. Response <Count> element = 52. Full PMID list and titles retrieved via esummary and archived in the task workspace. QueryTranslation returned by PubMed shows GPT*[tiab] was interpreted as an untruncated 'gpt'[Title/Abstract] search (PubMed disables automatic right-truncation for terms under 4 characters), which is PubMed's own documented behavior for this exact string, not an error introduced here; the count is what a user running this literal string on PubMed today actually gets.

scopus.query: TITLE-ABS-KEY("large language model*" OR "large language models" OR LLM OR LLMs OR GPT* OR "generative pretrained transformer*" OR "foundation model*") AND TITLE-ABS-KEY("brain-computer interface*" OR "brain computer interface*" OR BCI OR BCIs OR "P300 speller*" OR "P300-based speller*" OR "augmentative and alternative communication" OR AAC)
scopus.access_method: Attempted Elsevier Scopus Search API (api.elsevier.com/content/search/scopus) and the scopus.com web results interface.
scopus.provenance: API call returned HTTP 401 AUTHENTICATION_ERROR / Invalid API Key (no institutional API key available in this environment); the scopus.com web UI returned HTTP 403 Forbidden (requires institutional/personal login). No count obtained. Not invented; recorded null per instructions.

ieee_xplore.query: ("Full Text & Metadata":"large language model*" OR "Full Text & Metadata":"large language models" OR "Full Text & Metadata":LLM OR "Full Text & Metadata":LLMs OR "Full Text & Metadata":GPT) AND ("Full Text & Metadata":"brain-computer interface*" OR "Full Text & Metadata":"brain computer interface*" OR "Full Text & Metadata":BCI OR "Full Text & Metadata":"P300 speller*" OR "Full Text & Metadata":"augmentative and alternative communication")
ieee_xplore.access_method: Attempted IEEE Xplore Metadata API (ieeexploreapi.ieee.org/api/v1/search/articles) and the ieeexplore.ieee.org web search UI.
ieee_xplore.provenance: API call returned HTTP 403 'Developer Inactive' (no registered/active IEEE API key available in this environment); the web search UI returned HTTP 418 to the fetch tool (bot-blocked). No count obtained. Not invented; recorded null per instructions.

arxiv.query: (large language model OR large language models OR LLM OR LLMs OR GPT) AND (brain-computer interface OR brain computer interface OR BCI OR P300 speller OR augmentative and alternative communication OR AAC)
arxiv.access_method: arXiv API (export.arxiv.org/api/query), free-text search_query built as (abs:"large language model" OR abs:"large language models" OR abs:LLM OR abs:LLMs OR abs:GPT) AND (abs:"brain-computer interface" OR abs:"brain computer interface" OR abs:BCI OR abs:"P300 speller" OR abs:"augmentative and alternative communication" OR abs:AAC), restricted with submittedDate:[19910101000000 TO 20260719235959] to match the stated inception-to-2026-07-19 window.
arxiv.provenance: Live query executed 2026-08-03. opensearch:totalResults = 80; full entry list (id, submitted date, title) retrieved and archived. A first pass without the submittedDate filter returned 83 (includes 3 records published after 2026-07-19, up to 2026-07-31); the date-restricted rerun (80) is the number reported here as it matches the stated search window. Max published date among the 80 returned entries is 2026-07-14, confirming the filter worked.

biorxiv.query: the same term combination as arXiv, entered as a free-text abstract search under bioRxiv's own search interface (per eMethods S9)
biorxiv.access_method: bioRxiv's native search interface (www.biorxiv.org/search/...) was NOT directly accessible: both curl and the WebFetch tool were blocked by a Cloudflare managed-challenge / bot-protection page (HTTP 403, 'Just a moment...' JS challenge) that cannot be solved without a browser. As a documented fallback, bioRxiv content was instead queried through the Europe PMC REST API (www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search), restricted to preprints with PUBLISHER:"bioRxiv" (Europe PMC indexes bioRxiv's full corpus and is a recognized, real, independently queryable index of bioRxiv content, not bioRxiv's own search box).
biorxiv.provenance: Live query executed 2026-08-03: query = (ABSTRACT:"large language model" OR ABSTRACT:"large language models" OR ABSTRACT:LLM OR ABSTRACT:LLMs OR ABSTRACT:GPT) AND (ABSTRACT:"brain-computer interface" OR ABSTRACT:"brain computer interface" OR ABSTRACT:BCI OR ABSTRACT:"P300 speller" OR ABSTRACT:"augmentative and alternative communication" OR ABSTRACT:AAC) AND SRC:PPR AND PUBLISHER:"bioRxiv" AND FIRST_PDATE:[1900-01-01 TO 2026-07-19]. hitCount = 5; all 5 returned records verified via resultType=core to carry bookOrReportDetails.publisher = 'bioRxiv' (i.e., genuinely bioRxiv preprints, not medRxiv or another server). CAVEAT: Europe PMC's abstract-field search and bioRxiv's own site search do not necessarily use identical indexing/tokenization, so this figure should be read as 'bioRxiv records found via Europe PMC's index of bioRxiv,' a real and checkable number, but not guaranteed identical to what bioRxiv's own search box would return if it were reachable.

records_identified_total_note: Sum of PubMed (52) + arXiv (80) + bioRxiv (5) = 137. Scopus and IEEE Xplore are null (inaccessible in this environment; see per-database notes), so this total covers 3 of the 5 databases named in eMethods S9, not all five. A true 5-database identified count cannot be reported without Scopus/IEEE institutional access; do not treat 137 as the full search yield.
records_after_dedup_note: Computed by actually retrieving full title lists for all 137 accessible-database records and cross-matching them, not estimated. Two duplicate-detection passes: (1) exact-title match (case/punctuation-normalized) within and across PubMed/arXiv/bioRxiv found 5 duplicate clusters removing 6 records (e.g., PMID 38811613 'ChineseEEG...' = bioRxiv PPR805366, an exact-title preprint/journal pair; two PubMed records, PMID 38738213 and 37986728, sharing one title, both duplicating arXiv 2311.03611). (2) A targeted (non-exhaustive) author-verification check on the closest-titled remaining pairs found 3 further preprint-vs-retitled-published duplicates, confirmed by exact author-list match: PubMed 41698950 (ChatBCI, Hong/Wang/Najafizadeh) = arXiv 2411.15395; PubMed 40648241 (Caria, Sensors 2025 = manuscript ref 9) = arXiv 2412.07355; PubMed 39487163 (Cai et al, eye-gaze-typing/ALS retitling) = arXiv 2312.01532 (Cai et al, 16-author exact match). Total duplicates removed = 6 + 3 = 9; 137 - 9 = 128. This second pass was targeted at visibly similar titles, not an exhaustive pairwise author check of all 137 records, so 128 is a defensible lower-bound refinement, not a guaranteed-exhaustive unique count; a small number of additional unflagged preprint/journal pairs may remain among the other records. Scopus/IEEE records are excluded throughout since they were never obtained.
records_screened_title_abstract_note: Equal to records_after_dedup by definition: every deduplicated record was screened at the title/abstract level (see full ranked list with source IDs in the task-3 report). This equality is not a separately measured number, it follows from what 'screened' means once the deduplicated candidate set is fixed.
records_assessed_full_text_note: Reconstructed researcher judgment, not an originally logged count (matching the manuscript's own disclosure that screening counts were not systematically logged at the time). Method: each of the 128 deduplicated titles was classified as topically on-topic (core subject = an LLM/foundation-model/GPT-family model used for text generation, completion, or correction within a P300 speller, communication BCI, or AAC device/pipeline; or brain-to-text/EEG-to-text/fMRI-to-text decoding producing language output; or a review/editorial explicitly framing the LLM-BCI/LLM-AAC convergence) versus off-topic (general non-linguistic EEG/BCI decoding with no text-generation component, or a term-collision false positive, most conspicuously a cluster of 'AAC' hits that are really 'Automated Audio Captioning' or audio-codec papers unrelated to augmentative-and-alternative-communication, plus unrelated hits such as tumor-homing-peptide, urban-industry-bibliometrics, and circumcision-follow-up papers that matched only on isolated acronym collisions). 63 raw records were judged on-topic by this rule; 3 of those raw records are duplicate copies of an already-counted paper (the ChatBCI, Caria, and Cai-et-al pairs described above), giving 60 unique on-topic papers. The full per-title classification is in the task-3 report for audit.
records_included_evidence_synthesis_note: Firm, not a fresh judgment call: this counts the unique papers from manuscript.md's own reference list (references 1-14, Crossref/arXiv/bioRxiv-verified) that are both (a) cited in the Introduction/Discussion passage supporting the 'Evidence before this study' claim about prior LLM-BCI-speller/AAC integration studies (refs 4-12), and (b) actually present among the 128 deduplicated records retrieved by this exact search. Matches, verified by exact DOI/arXiv-ID: ref 4 (Gorenshtein et al 2026 systematic review, PMID 42202831), ref 5 (Lebedev et al, bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.11.06.686984, = PPR1116152), ref 6 (Parthasarathy et al 'near-optimal', bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.10.28.685216, = PPR1110651), ref 7 (Parthasarathy et al cross-subject training, arXiv:2410.15161), ref 9 (Caria, Sensors 2025 / arXiv:2412.07355, PMID 40648241), ref 10 (Jiang et al Neural Spelling, arXiv:2501.17489, PMID 42102075). Three other refs cited in the same passage were checked and confirmed NOT retrieved by this search: ref 8 (Valencia et al, ACM CHI '23 proceedings paper, not indexed in PubMed/arXiv/bioRxiv), ref 11 (Jo et al 'Are EEG-to-text models working?', arXiv:2405.06459) and ref 12 (Wang et al 'Escaping the BLEU trap', arXiv:2603.03312), both absent from the 128-record retrieved set, most likely because their titles/abstracts use 'EEG-to-text' terminology without the literal BCI/P300/AAC or LLM/GPT strings the search required. This 3-reference gap is itself an honest, checkable finding about the search's sensitivity, not a gap in this counting exercise.
limitations: Scopus and IEEE Xplore records_identified are null: both require credentials/institutional access not available in this environment. The identified/dedup/screened totals in this file cover only 3 of the 5 databases named in eMethods S9. If Scopus/IEEE access becomes available, this file should be rerun and eMethods S9 updated again.

The bioRxiv count was obtained via Europe PMC's index of bioRxiv content rather than bioRxiv's own search interface, which returned a Cloudflare bot-protection challenge to every automated access attempt in this environment.

records_assessed_full_text is a reconstructed topical-relevance judgment applied after the fact to the real retrieved titles, not a number that was logged during an actual full-text reading pass; it is reproducible from the classification list in the task-3 report but is a judgment call, not a measurement.

The near-duplicate (retitled preprint-to-publication) search was targeted at visibly similar titles among the 131 exact-title-deduplicated records, not an exhaustive pairwise author cross-check of all 137 raw records; records_after_dedup (128) is a defensible refinement, not a certified exhaustive count.
